q:
What is the output?
console.log([10, 9, 1].sort());
exp: sort() without a comparator compares elements as strings: "1" < "10" < "9".

q: What is the specificity (ids-classes-elements) of the selector ul li.active a#link?
exp: One id (#link), one class (.active) and three element names (ul, li, a) give 1-1-3.

q: Which HTTP status code means "Method Not Allowed"?
exp: 405 indicates the method is known but not supported for the resource.

q: A button inside a div; both have click handlers and the event bubbles. When the button is clicked, the handlers execute in the order:
exp: In the bubbling phase the event travels from the target up to its ancestors.

q: Which of the following is NOT a valid JSON value type?
exp: JSON supports object, array, string, number, boolean and null; functions are not allowed.

q:
Statement I: REST is an architectural style rather than a protocol.
Statement II: SOAP messages can be transported only over HTTP.
Which is correct?
exp: SOAP is protocol-independent and can run over SMTP, TCP etc., so Statement II is false.

q: In PHP, which statement includes a file and stops the script with a fatal error if the file cannot be found?
exp: require produces a fatal error on failure; include only gives a warning.

q: An inverted index used by search engines maps:
options: each IP address to a domain
each URL to its file size
each term to the list of documents containing it
exp: An inverted index stores, for every word, the documents (and positions) where it occurs.

q: If the viewport is 1200px wide, what is the width of an element set to width: 10vw?
exp: 1vw is 1% of viewport width, so 10vw = 120px.

q: Which organisation develops and maintains the CSS specifications?
exp: The World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) publishes the CSS standards; IETF handles HTTP RFCs.

q: Which HTML element groups related form controls and draws a box around them?
exp: <fieldset> groups controls; <legend> supplies its caption.

q:
What is the output?
console.log(typeof [] + typeof {});
exp: Both arrays and plain objects give typeof "object", so the strings concatenate to objectobject.

q: HTTPS provides confidential communication between browser and server by using:
exp: HTTPS is HTTP carried over a TLS (formerly SSL) encrypted channel.

q: According to the same-origin policy, two URLs have the same origin if they share the same:
exp: Origin is defined as the combination of protocol (scheme), host name and port.

q:
Match the CSS properties with their purpose:
P. opacity   Q. z-index   R. overflow
1. Stacking order of positioned elements
2. Transparency level
3. Handling content that exceeds its box
exp: opacity sets transparency, z-index sets stacking order and overflow controls content spilling out of the box.

q: Which protocol is commonly used to upload website files to a hosting server, using TCP port 21 for control?
exp: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) uses port 21 for its control connection.

q: Which technology defines the structure and data types of an XML document and is itself written in XML syntax?
exp: XSD is an XML-based schema language; a DTD uses non-XML syntax.

q: A form collects a user's password. Which method is more appropriate and why?
options: POST, because the data is not displayed in the URL
HEAD, because it has no body
exp: POST sends data in the request body, so the password is not exposed in the URL or browser history (HTTPS is still needed for encryption).

q: After var li = document.createElement("li"); is executed, the new element:
options: is immediately visible at the end of the page
is automatically added to the first ul
exists in memory but is not in the page until it is inserted, e.g. with appendChild()
exp: createElement only creates a detached node; it must be inserted into the DOM tree to appear.
